out/frequency.txt.description: The 10,000 commonest German lemmas, commonest first.
out/frequency.txt.licenceNote: Permissive again as of 2026-07-30, and this time the declaration matches the build. It was CC-BY-3.0 while silently depending on the CC BY-SA treebanks: `make de` pass 3 re-ranked through the treebank lemma table (build-frequency.mjs:95), but derivedFrom listed only Leipzig, so the contamination check had nothing to fire on. Measured exposure before the fix: 3,824 of 10,000 entries differed from the pure-Leipzig ranking, 47% of entries had counts moved by the table, and 85 strings never occurred in Leipzig at all. The lemma table is now Wikidata Lexemes (CC0), the treebanks are gone from the pipeline entirely, and build-frequency drops any key not attested in the corpora — so every string here occurs in CC BY Leipzig text.

publish.corpusSummary: 300,000 sentences of German news (2024) and 300,000 of German web text (2021) from the Leipzig Corpora Collection
publish.registerCaveat: These corpora are news and web text, so the list over-weights politics, sport and economics and under-weights conversation. For spoken or everyday German, weight it against a spoken corpus.

out/lemmas.tsv.description: Inflected surface forms mapped to their lemma, from Wikidata Lexemes (CC0).
out/lemmas.tsv.publishNote: ⚠️ WAS CC BY-SA AND UNPUBLISHABLE. It came from the UD treebanks, so share-alike would have contaminated any permissive artefact bundled with it. Rebuilt from Wikidata Lexemes (CC0) on 2026-07-30, so that constraint is gone: CC0 imposes no share-alike and expressly waives EU sui generis database rights, which CC BY-SA does not. Leipzig is in derivedFrom because the table is filtered to forms the corpora actually attest — attribution is owed, share-alike is not.

sources.name: Leipzig Corpora Collection — deu_news_2024_300K
sources.note: VERIFIED 2026-07-30 from Leipzig's own terms page (wortschatz-leipzig.de/en/usage) via the Wayback Machine, the archives themselves being licence-free and the live page bot-gated. The page carries TWO grants in adjacent sentences: "...licensed under the Creative Commons License CC BY-NC. [...] All corpora provided for download are licensed under CC BY." CC BY-NC governs the QUERY PORTAL; the download tarballs — which is what this repo fetches — are CC BY. That distinction is what the earlier CC BY-NC claim got wrong: a scope error, not a licence change. The wording is identical in every snapshot from 2017-04-06 to 2026-02-06, so both the 2022 and 2025 downloads are covered. Version 4.0 confirmed from the href on "CC BY" (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), not assumed — the visible text gives no version. ⚠️ ONE UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY, recorded rather than smoothed over: Leipzig's own CLARIN repository (repo.data.saw-leipzig.de) labels 87 LCC records CC BY-NC 4.0. None of the corpora used here are among them, and it is a different packaging on a different channel with its own stated NC default — but it is an inconsistency AT THE SOURCE. Given this project has had the Leipzig licence wrong twice, one email asking LCC to confirm CC BY 4.0 for the tarballs and explain that discrepancy is worth ten minutes before a public release.

sources.name: Wikidata Lexemes — German (Q188)
sources.note: Wikidata:Copyright, read 2026-07-30: "All structured data from the main, Property, Lexeme, and EntitySchema namespaces is available under the Creative Commons CC0 License." CC0 is a CONTRIBUTION requirement, so there is no upstream inheritance to chase — the usual code-licence-vs-data-licence trap does not apply. It also waives EU sui generis database rights explicitly, which every CC BY-SA alternative leaves open. 241,967 German lexemes in the dump of 2026-07-29. Replaced UD_German-GSD and UD_German-HDT, which were CC BY-SA 4.0 and are no longer used by any target.
